This is not a myth. This is published marine biology. Lobsters produce unlimited telomerase—the enzyme that rebuilds telomeres after every cell division. Their cells never receive the signal to stop regenerating. They are biologically immortal.

The Turritopsis dohrnii jellyfish reverses its own aging process entirely. When damaged or old, it reverts back to its juvenile polyp stage and begins life again. It has been doing this for 500 million years. It cannot die of old age. It is literally immortal.

The naked mole rat lives 10 times longer than any rodent its size. It shows zero increase in mortality rate as it ages. Its cancer rate is effectively zero. Its cells do not deteriorate.

Greenland sharks live over 500 years. Bowhead whales over 200. Giant tortoises over 190.

Nature solved aging millions of years ago. In dozens of species. Through dozens of different mechanisms. The genetic code for indefinite cellular regeneration exists throughout the animal kingdom.

And it exists in you.

Human DNA contains the telomerase gene. It is active in your stem cells and reproductive cells right now—keeping them young indefinitely. The rest of your body ages because that gene is selectively silenced in somatic cells.

Not missing. Silenced.

The question is not “can humans stop aging?” The question is “why was the off-switch installed, and who benefits from keeping it on?”

🖥 Colombia vs. Portugal: Injuries, predicted lineups & how to watch

📌 Get ready for Colombia vs Portugal in the 2026 World Cup! Discover the predicted lineup, injury news, and how to watch this Group K decider.

Colombia and Portugal meet in a huge Group K showdown with first place on the line at Hard Rock Stadium. Colombia have taken maximum points from their opening two matches and need only a draw to stay top, while Portugal must win to leapfrog them into first. With Cristiano Ronaldo back among the goals and Colombia carrying real momentum, this World Cup match preview has all the ingredients of a high-level group-stage decider between two genuine contenders.
​
Portugal have one notable concern in defence, with Tomas Araujo considered a doubt after picking up an injury in the opening match against Congo DR. Otherwise, Roberto Martinez has a strong squad available and is expected to keep Cristiano Ronaldo through the middle after his brace against Uzbekistan. Bernardo Silva and Rafael Leao are pushing for places, but Joao Felix may have done enough to keep his starting role in attack.
​
Colombia’s main injury news centers on Luis Suarez, who was forced off against Congo DR with a shoulder issue. The expectation, though, is that he will be fit enough to lead the line. Nestor Lorenzo could keep faith with the same side that won the first two matches, with Luis Diaz, James Rodriguez, and Jefferson Lerma all set to remain key figures. There is also set to be another start in central defence for Davinson Sanchez.
​
Colombia sits on six points and is riding high after two convincing opening performances.
​
Portugal responded emphatically to their opening draw, and the rout of Uzbekistan underlined the attacking quality in Martinez’s side.
​
The key trend is simple: these teams have only met once before, and this will be their first competitive encounter.
​
Colombia’s position at the top of Group K is deserved — they’ve been compact, direct, and dangerous on the counter, with Díaz a constant menace and Muñoz adding goals from deep. The knowledge that a draw is enough gives Lorenzo flexibility in how he sets his team up, and the enormous Colombian support expected at Hard Rock Stadium — given the city’s large Colombian community — will only add to that advantage.
​
Portugal, however, are no pushover. The 5-0 win over Uzbekistan showed what this side can do when the handbrake is off, and Ronaldo’s brace silenced those questioning his place in the eleven. The midfield trio of Fernandes, Neves, and Vitinha is among the most technically gifted at the tournament, and Lerma will have to be at his very best to contain them. Expect a tight, tactical contest — Colombia to hold their nerve and claim a draw, finishing top of the group.
